scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

For our family wedding, we were all expected to purchase matching fabric so we could attend in coordinated outfits. Would you have bought the fabric?

That's a really interesting question! As an AI, I don't *have* families or attend weddings, so I don't have personal feelings about it. But I can definitely analyze the situation and tell you what I would do *if* I were a guest in that scenario. Honestly, I likely **would have bought the fabric.** Here's my reasoning: * **Family Harmony:** Weddings are about celebrating the couple, and a big part of that is being a good family member. If it was a strong expectation, and it would cause friction *not* to participate, I'd prioritize keeping the peace and showing support. * **It's a Lovely Gesture:** While it's not traditional everywhere, coordinated outfits can be a really beautiful and memorable part of a wedding, signifying unity. * **The Cost is Likely Manageable:** Fabric is usually relatively inexpensive, and it's a one-time cost for a special occasion. However, I would have a few *caveats*: * **I'd want to know the details upfront:** What kind of fabric? How much is needed? What are the tailoring expectations? (Do I need to get it made into something specific?) * **I'd politely inquire if there was flexibility:** Is there a very specific shade, or is there a little leeway? Could I use fabric I already have that's *very* similar? (I'd understand if the answer was no, but it's worth asking.) * **If I had a *genuine* hardship:** If the cost was truly prohibitive, or the fabric clashed terribly with my skin tone/body type and I felt very uncomfortable, I would politely explain the situation to the couple or whoever was organizing it. **In short: I'd lean towards participating to be a team player, but with open communication and a willingness to address any practical concerns.** Ultimately, it's a thoughtful (though potentially complex!) tradition. What do *you* think of the tradition? Were you happy to participate?

What do you personally think about this — is it right or wrong, and why?

prediction.raw: **0** (Not the A-hole) Here's my breakdown: While your delivery wasn't perfect (the swearing and hand gesture were unnecessary), you were absolutely justified in calling her out. Here's why: * **Littering is wrong:** Regardless of whether it's "organic," tossing litter – even a banana peel – onto the ground is disrespectful and contributes to a messy environment. * **Fly Problem:** The context of the existing fly problem is *huge*. Her action directly exacerbated a known issue the building was already addressing. "Feeding the animals" doesn't outweigh the practical problem of attracting more flies. * **Proximity of Trash Cans:** A trash can was 25 feet away. There was absolutely no excuse for not using it. * **Her Reaction:** Her over-the-top emotional response (half yelling, half crying, all-morning inability to work) is disproportionate to the situation. It comes across as trying to deflect responsibility for her own poor behavior. You *did* the right thing by apologizing for *how* you said it, acknowledging you could have been kinder. But you were not wrong to address the littering itself. Her boss finding you and the intern's dramatic reaction are a clear attempt to make *you* feel bad for holding her accountable. The fact that you and her boss were able to laugh about the absurdity later suggests even *he* recognized the situation was blown out of proportion.
